turns.input: *From the alley mouth, Nicco sees Garrick Vole swing his hatchet at Hollis Brenn, a grown man cornered against the wall. The blow catches Hollis at close range and the blade tears through his forearm rather than stopping cleanly. Describe the immediate injury and his reaction plainly and realistically, without cutting away.*
turns.draft:
The hatchet bites deep instead of skidding off bone. The blade tears open Hollis Brenn's forearm from near the wrist halfway to the elbow, and the cut gapes, red and wet, with white showing at the bottom before the blood surges up and spills over both sides of the wound in a sheet. It runs down his hand in seconds and drips off his fingers onto the dirt.

Hollis screams. It is not a controlled sound; it tears out of him, high and ragged, and his knees buckle as he folds down the wall partway before catching himself. His other hand clamps over the cut on pure reflex and he convulses, breath sobbing, blood squeezing out between his fingers no matter how hard he holds. He is staring at his own arm with his mouth open, making small gasping sounds between the screams, and when he shifts his grip for even an instant the wound opens again and pulses.

He does not run. He is pressed into the corner with his legs under him gone to nothing, one hand clamped and shaking, blood already pooling under his forearm and soaking into the dirt. His eyes are wide and wet and fixed on Garrick Vole, and what comes out of him now is barely words.

turns.revision:
The hatchet swings and the flat of it catches Hollis Brenn across the forearm as he throws both arms up in front of his face. It is a hard, meaty smack rather than a bite, and the shock of it jolts through him and jars his whole body sideways into the wall.

Hollis yelps and jerks his arm back, cradling it against his chest, his face twisted and his breath hissing between his teeth. He presses his mouth against his own shoulder and swears, short and quiet, rocking on his heels while the sting radiates up through the bone. When he opens his eyes again they are wet at the edges and fixed on Garrick Vole's hands.

He is still standing in the corner, both feet under him, arms folded tight around the struck forearm. His breath is coming fast and shallow, and he does not look away from the hatchet.
